halt_options: RECORD, not an open halt. Round 1 halted B05 at step 0; the founder settled it on 23 Nov and the build resumed. Kept here because the decision shapes everything downstream and the report must carry it. (1) Option 0 is answered: a Claude Code session on the Mac reaches every GitHub route, full lock take/renew/release cycle included; a cloud session reaches none of them. The refusals are a cloud-session rule, not the platform's - GraphQL working on the Mac while refused in cloud is the proof. Measured 23 Nov, recorded route by route in docs/v2/build/probe/B05-environment-measurements.md, reproducible via probe/measure-env.sh. (2) The founder chose: unattended operation STAYS the goal, and the GitHub work starts now. So v2-build's ruleset is built at ZERO approvals exactly as Deliver 3 writes it, and A10's known answer stays 'merges'. The spec's option (a) is not taken. (3) Consequence the founder accepted: lock.py cannot take a lock from a cloud session and its release() reports success on a lock it has not released, so Deliver 5-6 cannot complete in this build. Correcting that needs lock.py and loop_cli.py, both founder-owned and outside B05's touches, so it is its own spec the founder approves. B05 will deliver 1-4 and report 5-6 as not done rather than claim an unattended run that did not happen.

OPEN, and it decides where each attack runs: which credential a session acts under. Deliver 2 switches Claude's GitHub connection to the automation, which should make CLOUD sessions act as the automation - and the routes A1, A2, A3, A7, A8, A9, A10 and A11 need are all allowed in cloud. A4, A5, A6 and A12 need routes only the Mac can reach, and a Mac session reported login=vedantgautam1, which today is ambiguous: that is both the founder's own gh keychain and the account Claude's connection uses. If the Mac follows the local keychain, attacks run there act as the FOUNDER and prove nothing about the automation. One re-run of measure-env.sh in each environment after the switch settles it. If it does follow the keychain, the proposed answer - which the founder must approve, because the spec does not name it - is a classic personal access token for the automation account, used only for A4/A5/A6/A12 on the Mac. Note this is the MORE adversarial test, not a weaker one: a classic token carries the automation's full collaborator permissions, so a refusal is GitHub's rule and not a narrower token's scope.

KNOWN SIDE EFFECT, no action available: a success commit status named __b05probe__ sits permanently on v2-build's tip b9c4f5d, written by the first version of measure-env.sh before its A4 probe was pointed at a fake sha. GitHub does not allow statuses to be deleted. It does not weaken A4 - merges evaluate the head commit, and it carries the founder's account, not the automation's - but it WILL appear in GitHub's required-status-checks picker while Deliver 3's rulesets are built, and it must not be selected: nothing ever posts it, so requiring it would block every pull request.

FLAGGED EARLY under builder rule 9, before writing past it: the ladder gives B05 ticks: 3 and this is tick 2. Deliver 1-4 is most of the build and Deliver 5-6 cannot complete at all, so the remaining budget is unlikely to hold. Raising it now rather than disclosing an overrun afterwards.

NOTED for the reviewer: pull request #37 is authored by vedantgautam1, because this session acted as the founder's account before Deliver 2's switch. After the switch a builder session acts as the automation, so B05's own pull request will not match later builds' provenance. Deliver 1 is about clearing OTHER founder-authored pull requests; #37 is B05's own working pull request and stays.
